facts.fact_text: The case concerns restrictions imposed by the authorities on the location of several public events.
The case concerns restrictions imposed by the authorities on the time of conduct of several public events.
The case concerns restrictions imposed by the authorities on the manner of conduct of several public events.
The three applicants in the present case were involved in a number of public events in 2007-2008 in Rostov-na-Donu.

In November 2007 Mr Nagibin and Mr Ye. notified the Rostov-na-Donu town administration of their intention to hold a static demonstration (picket) to protest against the authorities' decision to exclude the 'Different Russia' (Drugaya Rossiya) party from participating in the parliamentary election.
On 24 November 2007 Mr Nagibin proceeded with the static demonstration (picket).

On 19 June 2007 Mr Nagibin and Mr Ye. notified the Rostov-na-Donu town administration of their intention to hold a meeting of approximately three hundred participants on Sovetov Square from 5 p.m. to 6 p.m. on 30 June 2007.

On 19 June 2007 Mr Nagibin and Mr Ye. notified the Rostov-na-Donu town administration of their intention to hold the 'Dissenters' March' (Марш несогласных) along Sadovaya and Sovetskaya Streets following the meeting on Sovetov Square on 30 June 2007.
On 19 June 2007 Mr Nagibin and Mr Ye. notified the Rostov-na-Donu town administration of their intention to hold another meeting at Karl Marx Square until 7.30 p.m. on 30 June 2007.
Mr Nikolayev on various dates notified the Rostov-na-Donu town administration of his intention to hold public events at different locations as set out in the appended table.
On 24 November 2007 Mr Nikolayev and Mr S. intended to take part in the event organised by Mr Nagibin and Mr Ye. (the picket notified in November 2007 relating to application no. 37565/08).
On 8 December 2008 Mr Nagibin and Mr Ye. notified the Rostov-na-Donu town administration of their intention to hold a picket on Russian Constitution Day (12 December 2008).

The picket notified on 8 December 2008 was to take place in front of the building of the Presidential Envoy to the Southern Federal District on Bolshaya Sadovaya Street or across the road on Sovetov Square.
At 5.20 p.m. on 12 December 2008 Mr Nagibin came to Voroshilovskiy Drive for a solitary demonstration.
Mr Nagibin carried a sandwich board during his solitary demonstration on 12 December 2008 at Voroshilovskiy Drive.
Mr Nagibin distributed leaflets to passers-by during his solitary demonstration on 12 December 2008 at Voroshilovskiy Drive.
The case concerns restrictions imposed by the authorities on the location of several public events.
The case concerns restrictions imposed by the authorities on the time of conduct of several public events.
The case concerns restrictions imposed by the authorities on the manner of conduct of several public events.
The applicants complained about being unlawfully arrested.
The applicants complained about being convicted of various administrative offences.

The Rostov-na-Donu town administration replied to Mr Nagibin and Mr Ye. stating that if they intended to campaign for candidates of the association not listed on the electoral ballots they would violate the law.
The Rostov-na-Donu town administration requested Mr Nagibin and Mr Ye. to submit a notification in which the purpose of the picket event would be formulated in compliance with the law.

On 24 November 2007 Mr Nagibin was apprehended because his passport was found to be defiled with unauthorised pen writing and the police officers intended to draft the relevant record of the administrative offence at the police station.
Mr Nagibin was brought to a police station and charged with non-compliance with a lawful order of a police officer under Article 19.3 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

On 2 December 2007 Mr Nagibin was convicted of the administrative offence of non-compliance with a lawful order of a police officer on the basis of the police report and oral testimony of officer Mr Kh.
Mr Nagibin was sentenced to three days of administrative imprisonment.
On 20 June 2007 the Rostov-na-Donu town administration informed Mr Nagibin that the contemplated events had not been sufficiently prepared.
The Rostov-na-Donu town administration noted that the notification did not indicate which side of Sadovaya and Sovetskaya Streets the march would take place.
The Rostov-na-Donu town administration noted that the notification did not indicate where the participants would cross the streets.
The Rostov-na-Donu town administration imposed restrictions as to the location of the public event on each occasion that Mr Nikolayev submitted a notification.

Mr Nikolayev was told to follow the police officers to the district police station, with the stated reasons being that his driver's licence was a forgery, his cell phone had been stolen, and he looked like a wanted criminal.
Mr Nikolayev was brought to the Kirovskiy district police station on 24 November 2007.
Mr Nikolayev was charged with a breach of public order, an offence under Article 20.1 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
According to the police report, on 24 November 2007 Mr Nikolayev had sworn obscenely, disobeyed police orders, pushed the policemen away and attempted to flee.
Mr Nikolayev was found guilty of breach of public order under Article 20.1 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences and sentenced to ten days' administrative imprisonment.
On 8 December 2008 the Rostov-na-Donu town administration replied that Mr Nagibin had to hold the picket in another area, in front of the Sports Palace.
On 10 December 2008 the Rostov-na-Donu town administration again replied that Mr Nagibin had to hold the picket in another area, in front of the Sports Palace.
At approximately 5.40 p.m. on 12 December 2008 two police officers apprehended Mr Nagibin during his solitary demonstration at Voroshilovskiy Drive.
Mr Nagibin was taken to the Kirovskiy district police station following his apprehension on 12 December 2008.

Mr Nagibin was charged with a breach of public order and verbal assaults, an administrative offence under Article 20.1 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences, following his apprehension on 12 December 2008.

On 13 December 2008 the Justice of the Peace of the 6th Court Circuit of the Kirovskiy District found Mr Nagibin guilty of breach of public order and verbal assaults under Article 20.1 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The Justice of the Peace sentenced Mr Nagibin to three days' administrative imprisonment, to be calculated from 7.35 p.m. on 12 December 2008.

The Pervomayskiy District Court of Rostov-na-Donu found that Mr Nagibin's overnight detention had been lawful because the Code of Administrative Offences permitted detention for up to forty-eight hours.

On 8 October 2007 the Pervomayskiy District Court of Rostov-na-Donu found in favour of Mr Nagibin, Mr Batyy and Mr Ye. regarding the Rostov-na-Donu town administration's de facto refusal of their application to hold a march.
Following the Rostov-na-Donu town administration's appeal, on 21 November 2007 the Rostov-na-Donu Regional Court reversed the Pervomayskiy District Court's decision of 8 October 2007.

The Rostov-na-Donu Regional Court held on 21 November 2007 that the administration's response had not prohibited the meeting or prevented the organisers from submitting more detailed information on its route and venue.
The Rostov-na-Donu Regional Court held on 21 November 2007 that the organisers had not made use of the possibility to submit more detailed information on the route and venue.

The Rostov-na-Donu Regional Court determined, without referring to specific dates, that Mr Nagibin, Mr Batyy and Mr Ye. had missed the three-month time-limit for appealing against the Rostov-na-Donu town administration's decision.
